route_explored: Phase 1 gap 0: post-start time-ordered transport changes as an identifying implication, with one persistent unknown initial field propagated through all switches.
selected_subpattern: C10 (Characterize a Limit, Then Surpass It)
domain_thinness: C10's exemplars concern relational/combinatorial expressivity. Its exact-separation and no-already-published-surpass requirements apply structurally, but no gas-domain exemplar supplies a missing identifying construction.
difference_from_archived_route: The archived route attempted to restrict the admissible pre-start plume family. This route leaves that initial field unrestricted and asks whether the actual ordered post-start dynamics can expose source differences that a fixed transport operator hides. It neither renames prehistory reachability nor proposes a new controller.
bounded_derivation: In an illustrative known linear transport model, let c_A and c_B be two environmental concentration fields, d=c_A-c_B their difference, Q(t) the complete transport generator, and f(t)=q_A(t)e_s-q_B(t)e_sprime their source-forcing difference. Then d_dot=Q(t)d+f(t). The forcing amplitudes remain candidate-specific nuisance functions unless an independently supported release contract restricts them.

The executed stationary witness satisfies Q_old d_star+f=0 and hides d_star from the observed path. After a transport change, d_dot=(Q_new-Q_old)d_star at the switching instant if f stays the same. A nonzero derivative can break this particular witness only if its subsequent evolution reaches the actual observation path and survives the sensor-to-output map; it is not a sufficient source-identification criterion.

A source estimator would require that no physically admissible initial difference, source-strength histories, transport histories and sensor histories for a wrong source reproduce the same complete observed record. Even under a fixed known transport/sensor sequence, checking and exploiting this condition reduces to time-varying state-space observability or unknown-input identification; profile or Bayesian inversion then uses the same ordered response.
No new source world, trajectory, numerical counterexample or experimental result was generated for these algebraic observations.

naive_baseline_audit.runnable_version: Construct the ordered transport/sensor transition sequence, propagate each candidate source and an unknown initial plume through it, and jointly infer or profile source location, strength and initial state from the deduplicated gas record.
naive_baseline_audit.branch: i — the naive deployment version silently promotes sparse local wind observations or unstamped GMRF outputs into a known or calibrated joint full-field transport history, which the audited input interface does not provide.
naive_baseline_audit.domain_specific_obstacle: One moving sensor observes transport only locally at adaptively chosen positions while the source discrepancy can reside in unvisited cells, unknown ventilation or initial plume. Preserving time order does not derive the missing spatial/temporal transport law.
naive_baseline_audit.standard_tool_follow_up: With an externally supplied correct operator, the mechanism is conventional time-varying augmented-state inversion and does not surpass IASA's already ordered wind-conditioned response merely by retaining wind history. A new physically testable way to determine the source-relevant operator from the allowed local observations is required; no such construction was found in this bounded attempt.
excluded_repairs: Treat GMRF pointwise marginal covariances as independent, calibrated full-field trajectory draws.
Assume spatially uniform wind or known ventilation because that makes the switched system observable.
Choose constant source strength, a restricted initial plume, source-age bounds or zero boundary inflow solely to obtain separation.
Add an operator commutator score or an abstention rule and call it the M1 inference contribution.
Claim outperforming Bayes under the identical correct model.

method_grounded_checks.finding: Method Eq. 2 explicitly transports emissions by the intervening ordered wind history; Eqs. 4-6 align observations, project declared nuisance background and fit nonnegative source coefficients. Wind order or a rank/conditioning criterion alone therefore supplies no missing substantive step.

III-A explicitly states steady-state scope, while III-C Eqs. 12-15 use the physical dependency factorization and nuisance marginalization. Moving to transient history is a real scope change, but a known steady-state scope is not an unnamed assumption, and the required new valid transient identifying model has not been constructed.

hook_admission.surprising_empirical_reveal: A directionally surprising source-recovery prediction under the available observations was not obtained. Excitation improving known-model observability is already the obvious explanation, while no data-supported link from local wind variation to full source-identifying transport was established.
hook_admission.structural_reframe: The steady-state assumption is explicit in DGSE; temporal wind order is explicit in IASA. Re-describing either as a newly exposed tacit assumption would be inaccurate.
hook_admission.counter_intuitive_minimalism: Using the same online inputs does not itself qualify as a new mechanism; the proposed conditional computation requires a transport law stronger than the available contract, and no substantive source-inference simplification beyond occupied augmented-state/profile/Bayesian methods was established.
